guide.title: PagerDuty channel setup

steps.service: In PagerDuty, open Services → Service Directory and select (or create) the service McHarbor alerts should page.
steps.integration: On the service, open the Integrations tab, choose Add an integration, pick Events API V2 and save.
steps.routingKey: Copy the Integration Key (32 characters) into Integration (routing) key here.
steps.region: Pick European Union if your PagerDuty account is on the EU service region; otherwise leave United States.
steps.restKey: Optional: under Integrations → API Access Keys, create a read-only API key and paste it into REST API key to enable polling and incident links.
steps.inbound: Save this channel, open it again from Settings → Integrations → Communications and, under Ticket status from the ITSM, select Create inbound URL. Copy the URL; it ends in /api/incident-webhooks/ followed by a token. The signing secret shown beside it is not used by PagerDuty.
steps.webhook: In PagerDuty, open Integrations → Generic Webhooks (v3) → New Webhook, paste the inbound URL, scope it to the same service, subscribe to incident.triggered, incident.acknowledged, incident.unacknowledged, incident.resolved and incident.reopened, then copy the signing secret it shows once into Webhook signing secret on this channel (or into Signing secret issued by the ITSM).
steps.save: Save the channel and select Test connection. It checks the configuration and the REST key without paging anyone.
steps.testEvent: To prove the routing key, use Send Test Event on the PagerDuty integration page. McHarbor's test never triggers an incident.

guide.note: Alert grouping in PagerDuty can merge a McHarbor alert into another alert's incident. That incident carries the other alert's key, so McHarbor cannot read its acknowledge or resolve back; the alert still resolves in PagerDuty when it clears in McHarbor.
